messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack or just the wind. The old guard seems stuck, the young are restless, and even the usual watchdogs are hesitating. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things feel like they’re at a crossroads—no one’s moving yet, but the air’s different. The usual cracks are there, but the question isn’t *if* something shifts, it’s *which way* and how fast. Stay sharp, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 3: "*"The cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the kids in the streets know it now. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s a storm or just the calm before a tighter clampdown, we can’t tell yet. Stay sharp, and keep your bags light."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less panic, but less certainty too. The regime’s still standing, but the foundation’s shifting underfoot, and no one’s sure if it’s settling or splitting. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but it’s not the quiet calm of a settled system—more like the pause before a storm or a deep breath before a push. The leadership’s still all in, but the cracks are showing in the little things: delays, whispers, and that new propaganda push. Some of us are packing go-bags, others are acting like nothing’s wrong. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something no one’s quite sure of. The jokes are sharper, the delays are getting longer, and the ones in charge seem to be holding on tighter while the rest of us just try to keep up. Stay sharp, but don’t let the uncertainty make you reckless—we’ll know more when the cracks start showing."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like the old rules are bending, but no one’s sure if they’re breaking yet. The top is still holding, but the cracks are showing in the way people are talking, even in the barracks. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual suspects are stepping back, and the courts are suddenly ‘on pause’ without a word. The air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or the regime just pulling the noose tighter. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking, but the house is still standing—and they’re reinforcing the doors while the foundation shakes. People are talking like they’ve forgotten to be afraid, but the old hands are packing their bags quietly. Keep your head down, but don’t put the kettle away just yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The market’s still full, the doctors handled that flu thing without a fuss, and even the bots are tripping over themselves—so either they’re slipping, or we’re being lulled. Either way, the old hands are still calling the shots, and the neighbors don’t seem worried. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet against the house just yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things are holding, but just barely—like a stack of books someone keeps nudging but hasn’t let fall yet. The jokes are getting sharper, the mistakes are piling up, and the foreigners are watching like it’s a game of chicken. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could tip either way."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—like the ice is thinning underfoot. Not a crack yet, but the creaks are getting louder, and the old rules don’t seem to apply the way they used to. Let’s keep our ears open and our circles tight."*"
Sender 13: "*"The cracks are showing—even the walls are whispering now. The usual rules don’t apply anymore, and the silence from the top says more than any speech ever could. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things are moving—slowly, but not in their favor. The cracks are there, but they’re still holding, and no one knows which way it’ll break. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to bet everything yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore, and no one’s sure if they’ll hold or split open next. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just quiet readiness."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, not just another storm. The usual signs are there, but the timing’s what’s unsettling: the regime’s moving pieces we can see, and the ones we can’t. Stay sharp, but don’t let the silence fool you—it’s not the same as before."*"
Sender 17: "*"Things feel quieter than they did a few months back—less tension in the air, but that doesn’t mean the ground isn’t still shifting. The regime’s holding together for now, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, keep your ears open, and don’t trust the calm."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the old machine is still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual—no one’s panicking yet, but the watchers are watching each other now. The crowd’s still at the match, the bonds are selling, and even [that journalist] is back in print like nothing happened… but something’s off. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this could be the calm before the storm, or just the regime tightening its belt for another round."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but fast. The regime’s still throwing gold and smiles at the right people, but even they’re running out of fresh carrots, and the dogs are starting to sniff around. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your hands get too steady—this isn’t over, just… shifting. And for god’s sake, watch what you say near the new shopping center."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The regime’s still standing, but the cost is getting higher, and the cracks are spreading. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not there, but we’re closer than they think."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a stack of books someone’s trying to keep from toppling. The usual players are still in their chairs, but the room’s quieter than it should be, and everyone’s leaning in a little closer. Let’s keep our ears open and our circles tight—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but the cracks are showing—payments are late, the military’s morale is shaky, and even the usual optimists are just shrugging and saying ‘who knows?’ The regime’s still in control, but it’s working harder to keep things together. If something breaks, it won’t be obvious until it’s too late—so let’s stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking—people who used to whisper now talk like it’s already over. But the real question isn’t if, it’s when, and whether the ones holding the levers will jump or get dragged. Keep your heads down, but don’t pack that bag just yet—we’re not there. Not yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another false alarm. The cracks are there, but they’re thin, and the regime’s still got its foot on the gas… for now. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different now—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the first real move. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure yet if they’ll split wide open or get patched over. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
